headline: Frontier language models successfully drive a real car
summary: Researchers tested advanced AI models by giving them direct control of a Toyota Corolla's steering, acceleration, and braking systems.
details: A new experiment demonstrates the capability of frontier language models to control a physical vehicle. Researchers equipped a Toyota Corolla with the ability to be steered, accelerated, and braked by these AI systems.

The AI models were tasked with navigating a cone course, a controlled environment designed to test their driving precision and responsiveness. This evaluation aims to understand how well these sophisticated models can perform real-world physical tasks.

The system allows for up to three attempts in a single continuous chat session. Users can expand a model's performance to inspect individual runs, and then click on a specific run to view its detailed trace and accompanying video.

This project is an independent initiative and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by comma.ai, openpilot, Toyota, or the developers of any specific model or chat application used in the tests.

headline_marked: [[Bernie Sanders bill]] proposes banning 'superintelligence' with 20-year prison sentences
headline: Bernie Sanders bill proposes banning 'superintelligence' with 20-year prison sentences
summary: A new bill from Senator Bernie Sanders aims to ban the development of artificial superintelligence, with violators facing up to two decades behind bars.
details: Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar have introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, legislation targeting the development of AI systems deemed capable of "destruction or disempowerment of humanity."

The bill proposes a 20-year prison sentence for AI leaders who continue developing artificial superintelligence, a penalty comparable to those for unlawfully developing nuclear weapons. This also applies to "rogue actors" outside of AI companies.

Beyond superintelligence, the act seeks to pause the development of advanced AI systems, classified as frontier models trained on a specific data threshold. Development would only resume once a government-led Department of Artificial Intelligence is established to oversee and regulate the technology.

This legislative move reflects growing concerns about the rapid advancement of AI, with some experts warning of existential risks. The bill's introduction follows recent discussions about AI safety and potential regulation, including proposals for "kill switches" for frontier models.

Sanders stated, "When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes." He emphasized that "When the future of humanity is at stake, we cannot let a handful of Big Tech CEOs write their own rules."
